set_hash_algorithm: sha256 over the per-file sha256 hex digests, sorted by filename, joined with newline plus a trailing newline
runner: verified against aer-1/conformance.py check() and check_reference_profile() (kit v1.3.0) at freeze time

vectors.title: invalid timestamp
vectors.note: created_at is not RFC 3339. Core rejects; profile shape is unaffected.

vectors.title: empty fixture edge
vectors.note: Empty JSON object. Core rejects on missing required members. Note: a zero-byte file is harsher, it raises inside json.loads instead of returning reasons; fixtures must never be zero-byte.

vectors.title: future-dated receipt
vectors.note: created_at is a valid calendar date in the future. Core has no clock policy and accepts; freshness/replay windows are consumer policy, documented here as the honest boundary.

vectors.title: missing inputs
vectors.note: Canonical payload omits the inputs member. Core accepts (interoperability boundary), reference-producer profile rejects.

vectors.title: non-UTF-8 canonical bytes
vectors.note: canonical_bytes is valid base64 decoding to bytes that are not valid UTF-8. Both core and profile fail closed.

vectors.title: replayed receipt
vectors.note: Byte-identical resubmission of aer1-fv1-001. Core accepts: AER-1 core verifies receipt integrity, not ledger state. Replay detection is consumer/ledger scope, documented here as the honest boundary.

vectors.title: scope inflation
vectors.note: Receipt claims scope admin:* for a public execution. Schema-valid so core accepts: core does not adjudicate scope claims against reality. Scope attestation is producer-trust until the observer-attestation field lands.

vectors.title: tampered output, 1-byte change
vectors.note: One byte of the canonical payload changed (97412.55 to 97412.56) but output_hash still commits to the original bytes. Core rejects on hash mismatch; profile shape is unaffected.

vectors.title: valid minimal core receipt
vectors.note: Baseline valid receipt. Core accepts, reference-producer accepts.

vectors.title: wrong producer profile (non-object payload)
profile_reasons: canonical payload is not a JSON object
vectors.note: Canonical payload is valid JSON but a string, not an object. Core accepts (valid UTF-8, hash matches); reference-producer profile rejects. A different profile failure from aer1-fv1-005.
